terms.grammar: intransitive; with the dative of what is protested (ōrātiōnī), often impersonal passive (reclāmātum est) or ablative absolute (reclāmantibus omnibus)
evidence: Cic. Dom. 10: ab ūniversō senātū reclāmātum est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To shout against, contradict loudly: of a theatre, a senate, a whole province (Lewis & Short). The noun reclāmātiō is rare (Cic. Phil. 4.5).

terms.gloss: a formal protest: a tribune’s veto
terms.comment: The tribune’s stepping in to block a decree or a law; to make it is intercēdere with the dative (Traupman 181). It also means going surety for someone (Lewis & Short).
A false friend: post-Augustan, “declare, testify” (Lewis & Short), the older sense of English protest, not “object”.

phrases.english: the tribunes were re-elected over the consuls’ protests

sources: Lewis & Short: reclamo · Lewis & Short: reclamatio · Lewis & Short: intercessio · Lewis & Short: protestor
